binders: The proposition concerns a distinguished probability mass function on the real numbers.
In the third conjunct, p ranges over the nonnegative real numbers and hp assumes p≤1.
hypotheses: For the parameterized characterization, p is a valid Bernoulli parameter: 0≤p is built into NNReal and p≤1 is assumed explicitly.
conclusions: The distinguished real probability mass function assigns probability 1/2 to -1.
The distinguished real probability mass function assigns probability 1/2 to 1.
For every Bernoulli parameter p∈[0,1], pushing the Boolean Bernoulli(p) law forward by the map false↦-1 and true↦1 gives the distinguished real law if and only if p=1/2.
mathematical_definitions: The distinguished law is the pushforward of the Boolean Bernoulli(1/2) probability mass function by false↦-1 and true↦1.
PMF equality is equality of the complete probability mass functions, not merely agreement of selected moments or masses.
The values 1/2 in the first two conjuncts are ENNReal probability masses; the parameter 1/2 in the characterization is an NNReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The distinguished real-valued law is the symmetric two-point distribution taking -1 and 1 with probability 1/2 each. More precisely, a Boolean Bernoulli(p) variable transformed by sending false to -1 and true to 1 has this law exactly when p=1/2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The equivalence quantifies only over valid Bernoulli parameters p∈NNReal with p≤1.
The characterization concerns laws obtained by the fixed Boolean-to-real map; it does not quantify over every real probability mass function.
The target's main conclusions do not independently assert zero mass outside {-1,1}, although that support property follows from the supplied pushforward definition of the distinguished law.
The proposition is nonvacuous because p=1/2 satisfies p≤1 and realizes the distinguished law.
